13vat61: This week you review two classes: the quantifiers **alguno, ninguno, mucho, poco, demasiado** (with _cada, otro, todo_) and **double negatives** with _nadie, nada, nunca, tampoco_ and _ni… ni_. The situation: Paula and Tomás, two students from Tegucigalpa, visit the Mayan ruins of Copán with a guide.
dmay96: **Alguno** asks or states that there is **one or several**; **ninguno** says there are **zero**. They agree with the noun: _alguna tienda, algunos guías, ninguna entrada_.
1jmbbyu: Before a **masculine singular** noun, they lose the **-o**: _**algún** sitio_, _**ningún** problema_. Without a noun, they are full again: _¿Tienes algún mapa? —No, no tengo **ninguno**_.
o0dtln: **Ninguno / ninguna** is almost always **singular**, even if you'd use the plural in English: _No hay **ninguna** silla libre_ (there are no chairs).
axke32: Mucho, poco, demasiado: do they change or not?
1qoaznb: Before a **noun**, **mucho, poco, demasiado** agree like adjectives: _**mucha** gente, **pocos** guías, **demasiadas** escaleras, **demasiado** calor_.
p3jhpi: With a **verb** or an **adjective** they don't change: _Caminamos **mucho**_, _Los recuerdos son **demasiado** caros_, _Esta tienda abre **poco**_.
n21up7: **Muy** goes with adjectives and adverbs (_muy alto, muy lejos_); **mucho** goes with verbs and nouns, and also with **más, menos, mejor, peor**: _**mucho** mejor_, never _muy mejor_. **Demasiado** means "more than necessary" and is usually a criticism.
8p43fn: With a verb or adjective (doesn't change)
2emfhj: **Cada** never changes and goes with a **singular** noun: _**cada** escalón_, _**cada** día_, _**cada** persona paga su entrada_.
ppel0l: **Otro / otra / otros / otras** never takes **un** in front: _¿Me das **otra** botella?_ (not _una otra_). To say "one more", _otro_ is enough.
1agkdig: **Todo** agrees and takes **el / la / los / las**: _**todo el** parque, **toda la** mañana, **todos los** templos, **todas las** guacamayas_.
eiahzt: Double negatives: no + verb + nunca, nada, nadie…
1rqxp4x: In Spanish it's normal to have **two negatives** in a sentence. If the negative word (**nunca, nada, nadie, ningún, tampoco**) comes **after** the verb, you need **no** in front: _**No** fui **nunca** a Copán_, _**No** tenemos **ningún** mapa_.
yq5fv6: If the negative word comes **before** the verb, you **don't** use _no_: _**Nunca** fui a Copán_. The meaning is the same; with the negative word first, the sentence sounds a bit stronger.
16stn3o: You can put several negative words in the same sentence, always with just one **no** before the verb: _**No** le dije **nunca nada** a **nadie**_.
1rgbqxk: Two ways of making a negative
1o9zvne: _Nunca_ after the verb needs **no** in front.
1wukxcw: También or tampoco, and ni… ni
wtqaav: To agree with someone: if their sentence is **positive**, answer **también**; if it is **negative**, answer **tampoco**. _—Me encanta Copán. —A mí **también**_. _—No tengo agua. —Yo **tampoco**_.
19eha8n: To **disagree**: _—No me gustan las alturas. —**A mí sí**_. _—Yo quiero subir. —**Yo no**_.
1sr03of: To make two things negative together, use **ni… ni**: _No trajimos **ni** agua **ni** gorras_. If it comes before the verb, no _no_: _**Ni** Paula **ni** Tomás conocían Copán_.
uksjdj: Trick: check whether the other person's sentence has **no**. If it does, your answer to agree is **tampoco**.
1sms2t6: To agree with a negative sentence: **tampoco**.
1hsqos7: To make both things negative: **ni… ni**.

12raicb: The stress on the negative word
1vixh97: In a negative sentence, the negative word usually carries the **strongest beat** in the sentence: _No voy NUN-ca_, _NUN-ca voy_, _No vino NA-die_. The initial _no_ is short and soft.
iuvd9h: **Ningún** and **algún** carry the stress at the **end** (_nin-GÚN, al-GÚN_), which is why they have a written accent. **Ninguno** and **alguno** have it on **gu**: _nin-GU-no_.
cl4ix3: In short reactions, the important word comes at the end and the voice **falls**: _Yo tam-PO-co._ _A mí tam-BIÉN._ If it rises, it sounds like a question.
o9ejis: With an accent: **algún, ningún** (stress at the end). Without an accent: **alguno, ninguno, alguna, ninguna**.
kqhvfm: The reaction falls at the end: _tam-PO-co_.
